sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Nizam-ul-Mulk (Chin Qilich Khan)**: Appointed Viceroy of the Deccan (1713-1721, 1724-1748); founded the **Asaf Jahi dynasty** after defeating Mubariz Khan at the **Battle of Shakar Kheda (1724)**.
• **Maratha Expansionism**: Under **Peshwa Baji Rao I**, the Marathas sought to expand into the Deccan to collect **Chauth** (1/4th revenue) and **Sardeshmukhi** (1/10th additional levy).
• **Strategic Rivalry**: The Nizam played a 'double game'—sometimes supporting the Marathas to weaken the Mughals, and at other times inciting Maratha internal factions (e.g., supporting Sambhaji II of Kolhapur against Shahu) to maintain the **Balance of Power**.
• **Key Metric**: The **Battle of Palkhed (1728)** is the definitive military engagement where Baji Rao I outmaneuvered the Nizam using superior light cavalry tactics.

items.definition: Fiscal instruments used by Marathas to extract revenue from Mughal territories; Chauth was for protection, Sardeshmukhi was a hereditary right of the Maratha King.
Signed after Palkhed; Nizam recognized Shahu as the rightful Chhatrapati and agreed to pay Chauth/Sardeshmukhi.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Divide and Rule**: Nizam's policy of supporting the Kolhapur branch of the Bhonsle family to create a civil war within the Maratha state.
• **Peshwa's Northern Policy**: Baji Rao I's strategy to neutralize the Nizam first to secure the southern flank before moving towards Delhi.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Constant shifting alliances; the Nizam's reliance on French/British support later in the 18th century.
• **Solutions**: Maratha consolidation through the 'System of Tributary States' to stabilize the Deccan.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-B-D' (Palkhed, Bhopal, Duraha).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Palkhed (1728) led to Mungi-Shevgaon; Bhopal (1737) led to the Treaty of Duraha (1738).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Battle of Bhopal' (1737) with the 'Battle of Karnal' (1739). Bhopal was against the Nizam; Karnal was against Nadir Shah.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Geopolitical Realignment' to describe the transition from Mughal suzerainty to the Maratha-Nizam duopoly in the Deccan.

keyTakeaways: The Nizam-Maratha conflict was a struggle for the 'Deccan Subah' revenue rights.
Baji Rao I's military mobility rendered the Nizam's heavy artillery ineffective in open field battles.
The Nizam's survival was largely due to his diplomatic maneuvering between the Marathas and the British/French.
